title: Ind-Zariski maps are bijective on stalks
statement: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings and let $v:R\to S$ be a ring homomorphism. Assume that $S$, as an $R$-algebra via $v$, is the colimit of a small filtered diagram of commutative $R$-algebras $C_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], each with $R\to C_i$ a local isomorphism. A ring map $R\to C$ is a local isomorphism here if for every prime $q\subset C$ there are $g\in C\setminus q$ and $f\in R$ such that $C_g\cong R_f$ as $R$-algebras [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Then for every prime $q\subset S$, with $p=v^{-1}(q)$, the induced map $R_p\to S_q$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

lean.note: Exact existing statement, IndZariski.lean:581-588. Ambient binders: (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]. For the stated map v use v.toAlgebra, so algebraMap R S = v. Algebra.IndZariski is exactly the existence of a small filtered ColimitPresentation in CommAlgCat R with every constituent Algebra.IsLocalIso. The latter means that near every target prime the algebra is a localization of R away from an element. RingHom.BijectiveOnStalks unfolds to bijectivity of the canonical Localization.localRingHom at every target prime, equivalently its being a ring isomorphism. No new module or statement correction.
